reviewer.attestation: I independently inspected the submitted contribution, its source anchors, the live kernel/compiler/app/tooling implementations, and the named test coverage. Each decision reflects whether the proposed after-state actually remedies the claimed behavior.

findings: The live code preserves both the queued wait channel and caller window id; the proposed after-state hard-codes input and -1, so it creates the stated cross-window wake failure.
Selecting the smaller reader transaction and the maximum dirty LSN are the live oldest-snapshot and highest-dependency behaviors; both proposed inversions weaken recovery correctness.
The proposed return value and SDK argument swap turn the existing descendant rejection and source/destination forwarding into the reported rename corruption.
A zero context is not a live saved context, and the current epoch-plus-one assertion checks progress; accepting zero and weakening the assertion introduces the claimed fault.
The live greater-than update and less-or-equal test enforce forward durability progress; the proposed comparisons permit regression and unchanged metadata.
Both host and guest currently emit the canonical z prefix; changing their character values to y creates, rather than repairs, the specified parity drift.
The source explicitly accepts uppercase T; the suggested guest rejection and duplicate-Y classifier remove that supported spelling.
The present bound and strict overflow comparison admit an exact maximum while rejecting overflow; the after-state rejects a valid boundary in both surfaces.
The live runtime id and codegen mapping both identify rename; mapping it to reboot or service 58 is an intentional ABI misroute, not a repair.
The current codegen and SDK use the blocking wait service; the after-state substitutes a nonblocking read with a different ABI.
The app-spawn mapping and child-slot/child-pid order are already coherent; the proposed legacy target and swapped arguments cause the alleged launch error.
The zero branch deliberately selects the base-27 alphabet and the test exercises 0z27; changing both to base-81 removes the stated coverage and behavior.
Yield is consistently the zero-argument sleep alias in the live ABI; replacing it with sleep_ms changes arity and semantics while also redirecting the SDK wrapper.
The current full-span validation rejects zero/invalid spans and the SDK forwards pid then output address; the after-state weakens both protections.
The 1200-record cap matches the fixed five-word record window, and the live wrapper preserves pointer/count order; the after-state enables the claimed overwrite.
Separate old/new scratch bases and the invalid-pointer fuzz input are purposeful live safeguards; the after-state aliases buffers and weakens the fuzz case.
WINDOW_EVENT_WORDS is the required output span and the wrapper passes the caller base; subtracting one and adding one produce the described corruption.
The live non-positive fast path includes zero and os_sleep_ms calls its timed service; the proposed changes explicitly remove both properties.
Close requests currently use the dedicated request-close kernel and SDK paths; routing both through present destroys close-event delivery.
Teardown obtains the process pid before releasing pid-owned windows, and the host test requires zero windows; the proposal substitutes a slot and a vacuous assertion.
The current increment records successful app launches and the handoff test requires halt; replacing them with a no-op and no-trap condition weakens the implementation and test.
Compiler, manifest, and SDK consistently use reboot service 58; the suggested 59/rename substitutions manufacture an ABI collision.
The actual blocking branch records process state and returns SYS_BLOCKED, while the manifest documents code 2; the after-state falsely reports completed status 1.
getproc presently places its record length in payload r14 and reserves r15 for detail; both proposed swaps violate the published return convention.
The manifest and runtime already agree that sys_yield aliases sys_sleep; changing both to sys_sleep_ms is a coordinated regression, not supported behavior.
The manifest shell and bundled desktop entry both identify /bin/desktop; redirecting either to terminal contradicts the asserted desktop-first session contract.
The submitted after-state collapses the distinct task-manager and top aliases onto task_manager, directly contrary to its own path-separation invariant.
Paint is presently sourced and packaged as paint; changing its manifest source and builder identity to text_editor creates the reported app mismatch.
The live manifest and builder agree on /bin/doctor; replacing both with /bin/doc breaks the stable path instead of resolving evidence of drift.
The desktop manifest has init_desktop and the service description includes desktop sessions; removing both is the claimed regression, not a coherent repair.
Replacing knowledge status with graph changes the required check, and passing zero entries to os_ps removes the non-empty doctor probe described by the task.
The live registry field list and validator both require windowed; substituting stack_words removes the UI contract field rather than restoring coverage.
The graph walker correctly reads ctest_tests and the guest test treats zero as failure; both after-states weaken the claimed safeguards.
